questions.answer: Build in dependency order: organizer -> API reporter -> Flask -> FastAPI -> Postgres -> JWT -> scraper -> Excel -> scheduler. Each reuses the last and gives one interview story (problem/stack/tradeoff/demo).
questions.question: Why build the 10 projects in order? What does each add?

questions.answer: Flask uses Blueprints + app factory with manual validation; FastAPI uses Pydantic models, APIRouter, auto docs, and TestClient. Same task domain shows classic vs modern tradeoffs.
questions.question: Flask tasks API vs FastAPI tasks API tradeoffs?

questions.answer: Login issues short access + long refresh JWTs; protected routes use a Depends(get_current_user) that verifies signature/expiry and returns 401 on failure, with refresh rotation.
questions.question: How does JWT auth wire into a FastAPI project?

questions.answer: Trying to build everything at once yields no demo and hidden wiring bugs. Fix: smallest demoable slice (e.g. organize() or GET /tasks), test it, then extend with --dry-run/POST/DB flags.
questions.question: Trap: candidate starts the backend with Postgres+JWT+Docker on day one. What's the risk?

questions.answer: A nightly job without idempotency/--date reruns duplicates data on retry. Fix: --date flag, atomic write-then-rename, coalesce/max_instances, RotatingFileHandler logs.
